references.text: Continues Jesus' teaching on wealth and the kingdom of heaven, giving an illustration to emphasize the difficulties rich people have in entering God's kingdom.
Mark gives a parallel account where Jesus speaks about how difficult it is for the rich to enter God's kingdom.
Luke also provides a parallel account that highlights the challenges wealthy people face when trying to enter God's kingdom.
Isaiah warns against greed and self-satisfaction among leaders, which can be seen as related to Jesus' warnings about wealth.
The book of Psalms speaks of the blessing of trusting in the Lord rather than wealth, a theme that resonates with Jesus' message.
Hebrews encourages keeping life free from love of money and being content with what one has, reflecting Jesus' teaching.
